walkthroughs.body_html:
Geographical Debates — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Geographical Debates brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Geographical Debates.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why do some rivers form deltas and others form estuaries?
options: Race to the bottom is when companies offshore work to mines and underground factories.
Deltas form where rivers deposit sediment faster than the sea can remove it (calm seas, heavy load); estuaries form where tidal energy removes sediment (strong tides).
Deltas form on big rivers and estuaries on small ones.
Deltas form in cold climates and estuaries in warm climates.

mcqs.q: What is the 'race to the bottom' critique of globalisation?
options: The race to the bottom means TNCs compete with each other for the lowest prices.
Race to the bottom is when companies offshore work to mines and underground factories.

The argument that TNCs play countries off against each other, relocating to those with lowest wages, weakest regulation and lowest taxes — pressuring governments to cut standards to attract investment.
It is the process of rain falling from clouds.
Race to the bottom is when companies offshore work to mines and underground factories.
It is only water evaporating from puddles and lakes.
The combined loss of water from a surface through evaporation (from soil and water bodies) and transpiration (from plant leaves).
It is the process of rain falling from clouds.
